title: How the stack fits together
lede: Inspect each layer. The story is the data path: a person asks or a record arrives; orchestration decides the next step; models and knowledge interpret; compute is where those pieces run.

layers.label: Interfaces
layers.summary: Where people meet the system: boards, browsers, and approved business apps.

nodes.label: SWAN boards
nodes.role: Classroom and meeting display. Today: interactive panel, dual OS, presentation and teaching software. Proposed: questions against approved lesson materials, activity drafts, meeting-note assistance.
nodes.boundary: The board is on the local network. It only sends a prompt or document reference if a connector is enabled.

nodes.label: Knowledge assistant
nodes.role: A browser or in-app assistant for policy, procedures, and lesson materials. Answers should cite retrieved sources or say evidence is insufficient.
nodes.boundary: Queries stay inside the customer deployment unless an external search or ticket tool is explicitly connected.

layers.label: Orchestration
layers.summary: Self-hosted n8n sequences steps, retries, and human checkpoints.

nodes.label: Local n8n
nodes.role: Runs workflows: retrieve, validate, wait for approval, create a task, prepare a notification. AI may draft; n8n does not grant extra authority.
nodes.boundary: n8n can call local services only, or also external APIs if those nodes are enabled. External nodes can send data off-site.

nodes.label: Rules and approvals
nodes.role: Deterministic checks (required fields, amounts, roles) and a person who must approve before an action is taken.
nodes.boundary: Rule outcomes are recorded in run history. They do not require a language model.

layers.label: Models and Knowledge
layers.summary: Local language models plus a private retrieval index over approved documents.

nodes.label: Local LLM
nodes.role: Drafts explanations, extracts fields, classifies a request. Model choice depends on hardware, latency, and language needs. Not every model fits every machine.
nodes.boundary: Weights and prompts can stay on customer or JSI-managed private compute. Cloud fallback is optional and must be named in the design.

nodes.label: RAG index
nodes.role: Stores chunked, access-tagged documents. Retrieval returns passages with source references. Freshness and permissions are solution requirements, not extras.
nodes.boundary: The index contains copies of approved files. Deleting a source file does not remove it from the index until re-ingestion or a retention job runs.

layers.label: Compute
layers.summary: Where models, indexes, and orchestration actually run.

nodes.label: On-premises
nodes.role: Customer-owned room or campus. Highest control of data location; customer owns power, cooling, and access.
nodes.boundary: Data stays on site unless a connector is opened.

nodes.label: Managed private
nodes.role: Dedicated infrastructure operated with JSI under an agreed location and access model.
nodes.boundary: Location and operator access are design choices. They are written into the engagement, not implied by the word private.

nodes.label: Hybrid
nodes.role: Sensitive retrieval stays local; selected burst or update tasks may use an external service.
nodes.boundary: Anything that leaves the local network must be listed. Hybrid is not automatic privacy.
